head: Error
What happens
Example
rows: It runs but gives the wrong result

questions.q: Fix the logic error in the pass/fail program and write the boundary tests.
questions.model: I do: 'Pass' should include 50, so the condition must be mark >= 50. Boundary tests: 49 (Fail) and 50 (Pass).

questions.q: Pupil PDF: three buggy programs. For each, name the error type, fix it and write a test table (normal, boundary, erroneous).
questions.a: Program 1 syntax (missing colon); program 2 runtime (int of text, add validation); program 3 logic (wrong range); answers in the plan's key.
questions.model: The teacher fixes program 1: add the missing colon after the if condition; error type syntax.

questions.q: Extend: how can a try/except stop a runtime error from crashing a program?
questions.a: It catches the error (e.g. ValueError) and lets the program ask again.

questions.q: Stretch: why do programmers test boundaries on both sides?
questions.a: Off-by-one errors happen exactly at the edges.

questions.q: A program runs but gives a wrong answer: this is a ...
Back to our ponder: A program runs with no error messages but gives the wrong answer. Is it working?
questions.a: No: it has a logic error. Testing with planned data finds errors the computer cannot spot.
